summary: Iteration 4 backend validation: 10 NEW pytest cases in /app/backend/tests/test_push_and_maxspeed.py (TestSlidingWindowMaxSpeed, TestPushPublicKey, TestPushSubscribe, TestHelpPushDispatch) — all PASS. Full regression: 48/48 PASS. Covered: (1) 5-point sliding-window max-speed correctly bounds the reported max around real 50 km/h with steady 6-point traces, drops sub-5 km >250 km/h glitches entirely, and dilutes a 6 km / 5 s spike via the 4-leg window (max < 1500 km/h instead of the raw ~4320 km/h single-leg figure); (2) GET /api/push/public-key returns base64url string decoding to a 65-byte uncompressed P-256 point (no auth required); (3) POST /api/push/subscribe rejects anonymous (401), upserts by endpoint (no duplicates on repeated subscribe with same endpoint), persists user_id+keys+role; (4) POST /api/push/unsubscribe deletes the row matching endpoint+user_id; (5) /registrations/{id}/help returns {ok,status} promptly (< 5s) and never blocks on the background push fan-out — verified with zero subs AND with a stale subscription pointing at httpbin.org/status/410 that gets pruned from db.push_subscriptions after dispatch; (6) all responses JSON-serialisable (no _id leakage). FIXED a real backend bug while testing — see RCA section.

minor.issue: Endpoints that fail with non-410 transient errors (timeouts, 500s) are NOT pruned and have no retry/backoff — they just log a warning and stay in db.push_subscriptions forever. Consider a `failed_count` field and pruning after N consecutive failures.

Help fan-out excludes the requester themselves but NOT participants in OTHER events — query is correctly scoped to `event_id`. Verified. Just noting that if the same user has registrations in multiple events, only event-mates are notified, which matches the spec.

`asyncio.create_task(_dispatch_help_push(...))` schedules but never collects exceptions from the task. A bug inside the dispatcher (e.g. a malformed registration doc) would surface only as a 'Task exception was never retrieved' warning. Wrap in `try/except` inside the coroutine or use FastAPI's BackgroundTasks for cleaner observability.
PushSubscriptionIn.keys is typed as `dict` — no validation that `auth` and `p256dh` are present and base64url-safe. Garbage payloads upsert successfully and only fail at send time.

critical_code_review_comments: CRITICAL (now fixed): /app/backend/server.py line 526 previously did `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY = os.environ.get(...).replace('\\n','\n')` and passed that STRING to `pywebpush.webpush(vapid_private_key=...)`. pywebpush 2.3.0 interprets a string as either a file path or a raw base64-encoded DER key — not as PEM. Every push dispatch raised `ValueError: Could not deserialize key data ... ASN.1 parsing error: invalid length`, was swallowed by the generic `except Exception` at line 591-593, and the 410-pruning branch at line 587 was NEVER reached. Effect: push notifications were entirely non-functional and dead subscriptions accumulated forever. Reproduced with `python -c 'from pywebpush import webpush; webpush(...PEM string...)'`. Fixed by writing the PEM to a NamedTemporaryFile at import time and using the file path.

_stats_from_points sliding-window pass (lines 708-726) is correct: 4-leg window, only kicks in when len(legs) >= 4, falls back to total/total time otherwise. Verified end-to-end via 3 tests with realistic + glitch data.
VAPID_CLAIM_EMAIL falls back to `mailto:admin@example.com` if env var missing — fine, but consider failing fast in prod.
/api/push/public-key returns the raw VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY without any caching headers. Browsers will fetch on every subscription attempt — consider Cache-Control: max-age=86400.
All push-collection queries use `{_id: 0}` projection — confirmed no ObjectId leakage.

asyncio.create_task is fired in update_help (line 521) — Python may garbage-collect a strong-ref-less task; in FastAPI this generally works because the event loop owns the task, but adding a module-level set to retain references is safer.

rca of the issue:
BUG: Web Push delivery silently broken in production. ROOT CAUSE: pywebpush 2.3.0 changed how `vapid_private_key` strings are parsed — it now assumes a string is either a file path or a base64-encoded raw DER private key; PEM-formatted strings raise ValueError during ASN.1 deserialisation. The backend stored the VAPID private key as a PEM string in .env (with literal `
` newlines) and passed `os.environ.get('VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY').replace('\n','
')` directly to webpush(). REPRODUCTION: `from pywebpush import webpush; webpush(subscription_info=..., data=..., vapid_private_key='-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----
...
-----END PRIVATE KEY-----', vapid_claims=...)` → ValueError. IMPACT: Every help/SOS dispatch swallowed the exception via the generic `except Exception` and silently failed; the 410-pruning branch never ran, so dead subscriptions would accumulate indefinitely. MITIGATION (applied): write the PEM to a NamedTemporaryFile at module import and pass the file path to pywebpush. Verified: webpush now successfully reaches httpbin.org/status/410, raises WebPushException(410), and the row is pruned. Alternative cleaner fix the main agent may prefer: `from py_vapid import Vapid; VAPID = Vapid.from_pem(pem.encode()); webpush(..., vapid_private_key=VAPID, ...)`.
